agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — WP-03a verification: item (iii) EXTERNAL/TOOL-composite mechanisms mishandled
summary_for_principal:
This closes another checklist item from a past session (an earlier investigation's own detail was lost when this conversation's history was compressed, so I re-verified the claim from scratch rather than trust the label alone).

The document format supports two ways for a step to do its work that this system has never actually been able to run: one where an outside service does the work through a plug-in, and one where a step is really several smaller steps chained together. Declaring either one didn't cause an error — the system silently treated it as if a human or another AI assistant needed to do the work by hand, handing off instructions that, in one case, didn't even exist. No crash, just quietly wrong.

Fixed by refusing both cleanly, with a clear explanation, instead of the silent wrong behavior. Building either one for real needs decisions only outlined in the spec, not fully pinned down — I've written up exactly what's still undecided rather than guessing.

Full test suite: 376 passed, 5 new.

Numbered actions:
1. Nothing needs deciding right now.
2. Two items remain from the original list, plus two larger leftover pieces of an earlier item.

decisions.headline: D34 — mechanism.kind: EXTERNAL and TOOL (composite) are refused, at both validation (V17) and engine runtime, rather than silently dispatched as if they were a SKILL hand-off.
decisions.problem: Spec §12.1 states EXTERNAL and deterministic PROCESS are run BY THE ENGINE, the same side of the dispatch split as CODE — never handed off. _advance_step has no branch for either EXTERNAL or TOOL (composite): both fall through the generic mechanism.kind != "CODE" branch and are handed off exactly like a SKILL Tool. Wrong for both, differently: EXTERNAL should never need a hand-off at all; TOOL-composite has no ref (only composes), so the hand-off's own instructions_ref is silently None and composes's children are never dispatched by anyone.
options_rejected: Implement real EXTERNAL dispatch through a new domain port: rejected for this pass — §4.3's 'per adapter' wording names no operational contract, so implementing now means inventing the shape rather than reading it off the spec.

Implement real TOOL-composite dispatch by walking composes: rejected for this pass — §4.3's 'shared values' phrase, and whether a non-deterministic child's hand-off should surface transparently or stay opaque, are both spec-silent.
decisions.cost_to_change: Low — V17 and the _advance_step check are both simple early returns/refusals with no schema or durable-record shape change.
